controls.title: Determining the scope of the AI management system
controls.r: Determine and document AIMS boundaries and applicability, considering 4.1, 4.2 and the AI systems in scope.
controls.e: Approved AIMS scope statement, AI system list

controls.title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
controls.r: Assign and communicate AIMS roles, incl. responsibility for conformity to the standard and reporting AIMS performance to top management.
controls.e: RACI, AI governance charter, appointment records

controls.title: Competence
controls.r: Determine necessary competence of persons affecting AI performance; ensure competence via education, training or experience; retain evidence.

controls.title: Awareness
controls.r: Ensure persons are aware of the AI policy, their contribution to AIMS effectiveness and consequences of non-conformity.

controls.title: Documented information - General
controls.r: AIMS includes documented information required by the standard and determined necessary for AIMS effectiveness.

controls.title: Internal audit - General
controls.r: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to check AIMS conformity to own requirements and the standard, and effective implementation.

controls.title: Documentation of AI system design and development
controls.r: Document design and development per organizational objectives, documented requirements and criteria (architecture, model choices, training approach).

controls.title: AI literacy
controls.r: Take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of staff and others dealing with AI systems on the organization's behalf, considering their technical knowledge, experience and context of use.

controls.title: Authorised representatives
controls.r: Non-EU providers appoint an EU authorised representative with a mandate covering conformity documentation, cooperation with authorities and registration duties.

controls.title: International co-operation for trustworthy AI
controls.r: Actively co-operate across borders and sectors to advance responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI, incl. common understanding of AI actor obligations, interoperable governance, standards and metrics.
controls.e: Participation in international AI governance initiatives

controls.title: General-purpose and generative AI risks
controls.r: Address risks specific to general-purpose/foundation and generative AI models, incl. safety, misuse and information-integrity risks (e.g. disinformation, deepfakes).

controls.title: Accountability structures are in place so appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible and trained for mapping, measuring and managing AI risks.
controls.r: Assign clear roles/responsibilities for AI risk management and provide training.

controls.title: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility processes are prioritized, and organizational risk management supported by a diverse team.
controls.r: Ensure diverse, multidisciplinary teams involved in AI risk decisions.

controls.title: Example impact categories and considerations
controls.r: Consider the standard's example impact categories (e.g. individual, group, societal, environmental) and illustrative considerations when identifying impacts in 5.7.
controls.e: Impact category checklist used in assessments

controls.title: Competence
controls.r: Determine necessary competence of persons affecting security performance; ensure competence via education/training/experience; take actions and retain evidence.

controls.title: Awareness
controls.r: Ensure persons are aware of policy, their contribution to ISMS effectiveness and implications of non-conformity.

controls.title: Documented information - General
controls.r: ISMS includes documented information required by the standard and determined necessary for effectiveness.

controls.title: Internal audit - General
controls.r: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to check conformity to own requirements and the standard, and effective implementation.

controls.title: Management responsibilities
controls.r: Management requires all personnel to apply security per policies and procedures.

controls.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
controls.r: Regularly review compliance with policies, topic-specific policies, rules and standards.

controls.title: Screening
controls.r: Verify candidates' background before joining and on an ongoing basis per laws and risk.

controls.title: Terms and conditions of employment
controls.r: Employment agreements state personnel and organizational security responsibilities.

controls.title: Information security awareness, education and training
controls.r: Provide appropriate awareness, education, training and regular policy updates.

controls.title: Disciplinary process
controls.r: Formalize and communicate a disciplinary process for security policy violations.

controls.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
controls.r: Identify, document, review and sign NDAs reflecting protection needs.

controls.title: Remote working
controls.r: Implement security measures when personnel work remotely.

controls.title: Protection against malware
controls.r: Implement malware protection supported by user awareness.

controls.title: General
controls.r: Certification must inspire confidence: principles of impartiality, competence, responsibility, openness, confidentiality, responsiveness to complaints and risk-based approach underpin all certification activity.

controls.title: Competence
controls.r: Certification personnel must have the knowledge and skills to perform certification activities for the relevant scope/sector.
controls.e: CB team competence evidence, sector/technical-expert confirmation

controls.title: Risk-based approach
controls.r: The CB considers risks to impartiality, competence and consistency when planning and decision-making.

controls.title: Personnel involved in certification activities
controls.r: The CB has sufficient competent personnel (auditors, reviewers, decision-makers); contracts and training are in place.

controls.title: Personnel records
controls.r: The CB maintains up-to-date records of qualifications, training, experience and performance of personnel.

controls.title: Certification documents
controls.r: The CB gives certification documents identifying the client, standard, scope, and validity.
controls.e: Issued certificate verified against scope and SoA

controls.title: Support (privacy extension)
controls.r: Extend ISO 27001 7.x so resources, competence, awareness, communication and documented information also cover the PIMS.
controls.e: Privacy training records, PIMS documentation set

controls.title: People controls - privacy guidance
controls.r: Apply privacy-specific guidance to people controls (e.g. screening, terms of employment, awareness/training on PII handling, confidentiality obligations).

controls.title: Mapping annexes (ISO/IEC 29100, GDPR, ISO/IEC 27018 and 29151)
controls.r: Use the informative mapping annexes to cross-reference PIMS controls to the ISO/IEC 29100 privacy framework, GDPR articles, and cloud-PII-specific standards ISO/IEC 27018 and 29151.
controls.e: Cross-reference table used for GDPR/29100 alignment (see Tab 9 GDPR)

controls.title: Opt-in, not opt-out, for anything beyond the necessary minimum
controls.r: Any processing beyond what is strictly necessary (e.g. marketing, analytics, AI training on user data) requires an affirmative, informed choice rather than being pre-enabled.

controls.title: Communicate in clear, understandable language
controls.r: Ensure privacy-related information presented within the design (notices, prompts, settings) is written in plain, non-technical, non-legalistic language appropriate to the audience.
controls.e: Plain-language review of in-product privacy communications

controls.title: Communicating to diverse consumer population
controls.r: Ensure privacy communications are accessible and understandable across the diversity of the consumer population (language, literacy, disability, age, context of use).
controls.e: Accessibility/plain-language review of privacy communications across user segments

controls.title: Integrating design/operation of privacy controls into product development and management lifecycles
controls.r: Embed privacy-control design and operation activities into the standard product development and management lifecycle (e.g. stage gates, sprints, release processes), not as a separate parallel track.
controls.e: Privacy checkpoints embedded in the product development lifecycle

controls.title: Provenance of AI-generated content (related but distinct standard)
controls.r: Where the AI system generates synthetic content (text, image, audio, video), be aware that content-level provenance/authenticity (e.g. watermarking, C2PA Content Credentials) is addressed by separate, content-focused standards/initiative...
controls.e: Mapping of which provenance mechanism (ISO/IEC 5181 for data assets vs C2PA-style content credentials for generated outputs) applies to each AI use case

controls.title: Apply established information security practice as the foundation
controls.r: Recognize that AI systems run on conventional computer systems/networks, so all the usual confidentiality, integrity and availability/cybersecurity concerns (e.g. ISO 27001/27002, Tab 7) still apply and remain essential - AI-specific thr...
controls.e: Confirmation that existing ISMS controls (Tab 7) are applied to AI system infrastructure before layering AI-specific controls

controls.title: Further threats per the standard's catalogue (12+ scenarios)

controls.e: Full threat-catalogue review against the published ISO/IEC 27090 text

controls.title: Apply threat-specific detection and mitigation guidance
controls.r: For each threat in Clause 6, apply the standard's guidance on characterising the threat, its potential consequences, and how to detect and mitigate it - rather than applying generic security controls uniformly without considering threat-...
controls.e: Threat-by-threat mitigation mapping (one control set per threat type in Clause 6)

controls.title: Federated machine learning
controls.r: Apply additional considerations for federated learning architectures, where training occurs across distributed data holders without centralising raw data - a different trust and attack-surface model from centralised training.
controls.e: Federated learning threat model and controls, where this architecture is used

controls.title: Persistence
controls.r: Adversary maintains a foothold across restarts, retraining or redeployment of the AI system (e.g. a persistent backdoor embedded in a model or pipeline).
controls.e: Model/pipeline integrity verification across retraining and redeployment cycles

controls.title: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
controls.r: Identify interested parties relevant to the AIMS, their requirements (incl. legal/regulatory, e.g. EU AI Act, PDPPL) and which will be addressed through the AIMS.
controls.e: Stakeholder register, AI regulatory/contractual requirements register

controls.title: AI management system
controls.r: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the AIMS, including needed processes and their interactions.

controls.title: Leadership and commitment
controls.r: Top management demonstrates commitment: AI policy and objectives aligned to strategy, AIMS integrated into processes, resources provided, importance of effective AI management communicated, outcomes ensured, improvement promoted.

controls.title: AI objectives and planning to achieve them
controls.r: Establish measurable AI objectives at relevant functions/levels, consistent with the AI policy; plan what, resources, owner, deadline and evaluation.

controls.title: Planning of changes
controls.r: Carry out AIMS changes in a planned manner when a need for change is determined.

controls.title: Resources
controls.r: Determine and provide resources needed to establish, implement, maintain and improve the AIMS.

controls.title: Communication
controls.r: Determine internal and external communications relevant to the AIMS: what, when, with whom, how.

controls.title: AI policy
controls.r: Document a policy for the development or use of AI systems.

controls.title: Alignment with other organizational policies
controls.r: Determine where other policies (security, privacy, quality, safety, etc.) are affected by or apply to AI objectives, and align them.

controls.title: Review of the AI policy
controls.r: Review the AI policy at planned intervals or on significant change to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

controls.title: External reporting
controls.r: Provide capability for interested parties to report adverse impacts of the AI system.

controls.title: Information for interested parties
controls.r: Determine and document obligations to report information about the AI system to interested parties.

controls.title: Objectives for responsible use of AI system
controls.r: Identify and document objectives guiding responsible use, aligned to AI policy.

controls.title: Shaping an enabling interoperable governance and policy environment
controls.r: Promote a policy environment that supports agile transition from R&D to deployment, incl. mechanisms such as regulatory sandboxes to experiment with AI safely, and work towards interoperable governance frameworks.

controls.title: Environmental footprint
controls.r: Consider and where possible measure/reduce the environmental footprint (energy, compute, resources) of AI systems across their lifecycle.

controls.title: Organizational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk.
controls.r: Foster risk-aware culture, incl. incentives, policies for documenting risks/tradeoffs, and processes for flagging risks.

controls.title: Processes are in place for robust engagement with relevant AI actors (incl. external stakeholders and end users).
controls.r: Establish mechanisms to solicit and incorporate feedback from relevant AI actors.

controls.title: Planning the assessment
controls.r: Plan scope, resources, timeline, methodology and tools for each AISIA, proportionate to the AI system's risk and context.

controls.title: Integration with AI risk management and the AI management system
controls.r: Integrate AISIA outputs into the organization's AI risk assessment/treatment process and AI management system (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001 clauses 6.1.2 and 6.1.4).

controls.title: Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties
controls.r: Identify interested parties, their ISMS-relevant requirements (legal, regulatory, contractual) and which are addressed by the ISMS.
controls.e: Interested-parties register, legal/regulatory register (e.g. PDPPL, QCB/CRA)

controls.title: Leadership and commitment
controls.r: Top management demonstrates commitment: policy/objectives aligned to strategy, ISMS integrated in processes, resources provided, importance communicated, outcomes ensured, improvement promoted.
controls.e: Management minutes, budget approvals, sponsor communications

controls.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
controls.r: Assign and communicate ISMS roles, incl. responsibility for conformity and for reporting performance to top management.

controls.title: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
controls.r: Set measurable, monitored, communicated objectives consistent with policy; plan what, resources, owner, deadline, evaluation.

controls.title: Planning of changes
controls.r: Carry out ISMS changes (identified as needed) in a planned manner.
controls.e: Change records for ISMS, impact assessments

controls.title: Resources
controls.r: Determine and provide resources needed for establishing, implementing, maintaining and improving the ISMS.

controls.title: Communication
controls.r: Determine internal/external ISMS communications: what, when, with whom, who communicates, and process.

controls.title: Creating and updating
controls.r: Ensure appropriate identification/description, format/media, review and approval.

controls.title: Policies for information security
controls.r: Define, approve, publish, communicate and review the information security policy and topic-specific policies at planned intervals.

controls.title: Contact with authorities
controls.r: Maintain contact with relevant authorities (e.g. regulator, CERT, law enforcement).

controls.title: Contact with special interest groups
controls.r: Maintain contact with security forums and professional associations.

controls.title: Threat intelligence
controls.r: Collect and analyse information on threats to produce threat intelligence.
controls.e: TI sources, TI reports, use in risk/detection

controls.title: Information security in project management
controls.r: Integrate security into project management across all projects.

controls.title: Management of impartiality
controls.r: The CB identifies, analyses and documents risks to impartiality and has top management commitment to it.

controls.title: Organizational structure and top management
controls.r: The CB documents its organizational structure, duties and authorities; a body/committee safeguards impartiality.

controls.title: Confidentiality
controls.r: The CB keeps information about clients confidential, has a legally enforceable commitment, and informs the client before disclosing to third parties unless required by law.

controls.title: Client records
controls.r: The CB maintains records of audit and certification for all clients, kept confidential and retained per policy.
controls.e: Records retention and access-control rules for audit records

controls.title: Position of the DPO
controls.r: Involve the DPO properly and in a timely manner in all data protection matters; provide resources and independence; DPO reports to highest management level.

controls.title: Context of the organization (privacy extension)
controls.r: Extend ISO 27001 4.1-4.4 to consider the organization's role (PII controller and/or processor), applicable privacy laws/regulations (e.g. GDPR, PDPPL), and interested parties relevant to PII processing.
controls.e: PIMS scope statement identifying controller/processor role(s) and applicable privacy law

controls.title: Leadership (privacy extension)
controls.r: Extend ISO 27001 5.1-5.3 so the information security policy is extended (or a separate privacy policy established) with privacy roles and responsibilities assigned.

controls.title: Make privacy a stated organizational commitment
controls.r: Adopt a documented commitment (policy/charter) that privacy protection is a default objective of every product and process, with leadership accountability.

controls.title: Make privacy practices visible to users and stakeholders
controls.r: Ensure privacy notices, settings and data flows are clear, accessible and accurately reflect what the design actually does - avoid gaps between stated policy and actual behaviour.
controls.e: Privacy notice accuracy review against actual system behaviour

controls.title: Cyber threat information and intelligence sharing

controls.title: AI system verification and validation
controls.r: Define and document verification/validation measures and criteria (performance, bias, robustness, security testing).
controls.e: Test plans, V&V reports, acceptance criteria

controls.title: Human resources
controls.r: Document human resources and their competences for development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, and verification and integration of the AI system.

controls.title: Objectives for responsible development of AI system
controls.r: Identify and document objectives guiding responsible AI development (fairness, transparency, robustness, safety, etc.) and integrate them into the life cycle.

controls.title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models with systemic risk
controls.r: Perform model evaluation incl. adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track/document/report serious incidents, ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.
controls.e: Systemic risk assessment, adversarial test reports, incident log, cybersecurity measures

controls.title: Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied to AI risks, and effectiveness of metrics evaluated.
controls.r: Select and document metrics for measuring AI risks (performance, fairness, robustness, etc.).

controls.title: AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics: valid/reliable, safe, secure/resilient, accountable/transparent, explainable/interpretable, privacy-enhanced, fair with harmful bias managed.
controls.r: Test and document evaluation of each trustworthy characteristic, incl. security and resilience testing against adversarial/abuse scenarios.
controls.e: Test reports covering security/resilience, robustness, bias, privacy

controls.title: Feedback about efficacy of measurement is gathered and assessed.
controls.r: Gather feedback (incl. from red-teaming, external audits, user reports) and use it to improve measurement approaches.

controls.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
controls.r: Regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier practices and service delivery.
controls.e: Supplier reviews, SLA/security reports, audit rights

controls.title: Access to source code
controls.r: Appropriately manage read/write access to source code, dev tools and libraries.

controls.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.r: Obtain vulnerability info, assess exposure and take appropriate measures.

controls.title: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.r: Restrict and tightly control utility programs able to override system controls.

controls.title: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.r: Implement procedures to securely manage software installation on operational systems.

controls.title: Secure development life cycle
controls.r: Establish and apply rules for secure development of software and systems.

controls.title: Application security requirements
controls.r: Identify, specify and approve security requirements for applications.

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.r: Establish, document, maintain and apply secure engineering principles.

controls.title: Secure coding
controls.r: Apply secure coding principles to software development.

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.r: Define and implement security testing in the development life cycle.

controls.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
controls.r: Separate and secure development, testing and production environments.

controls.title: Change management
controls.r: Subject changes to information processing facilities and systems to change management procedures.
controls.e: Change tickets, CAB records, rollback plans

controls.title: Test information
controls.r: Appropriately select, protect and manage test information.

controls.title: Protection and prevention
controls.r: Implement controls: information security policies/procedures/access controls, network segmentation, encryption/cryptography policies, third-party access policies, change management, document management, patch management, and ICT project ...
controls.e: Security policy set, access control, segmentation, encryption, patch and change management evidence

controls.title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
controls.r: Perform a range of basic tests: vulnerability assessments/scans, network security assessments, source code reviews, performance tests, end-to-end tests, and scenario-based compatibility tests.
controls.e: Vulnerability scan, code review, performance and end-to-end test reports

controls.title: Align model testing with the 'secure and resilient' trustworthy characteristic
controls.r: Where model testing covers security-relevant behaviour (robustness to adversarial inputs, resistance to manipulation), ensure this is explicitly scoped alongside functional/accuracy testing.
controls.e: Test plan explicitly covering security/robustness alongside accuracy benchmarks

controls.title: Establish or engage a red-teaming capability aligned to ARIA's approach
controls.r: Build (or contract) a red-teaming capability able to rigorously challenge the AI system to surface weaknesses, consistent with ARIA's structured, scenario-based red-teaming methodology.
controls.e: Red-team charter/engagement scoped to ARIA-style structured adversarial testing

controls.title: Scope red-teaming scenarios against known AI risk taxonomies
controls.r: Design red-team scenarios informed by the NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile risks and, where relevant, the OWASP LLM Top 10 (Tab 10), so red-teaming coverage is traceable to a recognized risk set.
controls.e: Red-team scenario catalogue mapped to GenAI Profile risks and/or OWASP LLM Top 10

controls.title: Capture and remediate red-team findings
controls.r: Document red-teaming findings, prioritise by severity, and track remediation to closure, consistent with how ARIA expects materialized risks to feed back into system improvement.
controls.e: Red-team findings log and remediation tracker

controls.title: Understand CoRIx as ARIA's composite measurement instrument
controls.r: Recognize that ARIA scores evaluated systems on the Contextual Robustness Index (CoRIx), a suite of metrics (ARIA documents ten measurement dimensions, including the seven AI RMF trustworthy characteristics - valid/reliable, safe, secure...
controls.e: Internal summary of CoRIx dimensions relevant to the organization's AI systems

controls.title: AI system impact assessment
controls.r: Define a process to assess potential consequences of AI systems on individuals, groups and society through their life cycle; document and retain results.
controls.e: Impact assessment procedure and completed assessments

controls.title: AI system impact assessment
controls.r: Perform AI system impact assessments per 6.1.4 at planned intervals or on significant change; retain results.

controls.title: AI system impact assessment process
controls.r: Establish a process to assess potential consequences for individuals, groups and society from the AI system throughout its life cycle.

controls.title: Documentation of AI system impact assessments
controls.r: Document results of impact assessments and retain for a defined period.

controls.title: Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals
controls.r: Assess and document impacts on individuals/groups throughout the life cycle (e.g. fairness, privacy, safety, rights).

controls.title: Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
controls.r: Assess and document societal impacts (e.g. environment, economy, culture, public health, misinformation) throughout the life cycle.

controls.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

controls.r: Certain deployers (public bodies, banking/insurance, etc.) perform a fundamental rights impact assessment before deployment: process description, period/frequency of use, affected persons, specific risks, human oversight measures, and mi...

controls.title: Impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations and society are characterized/understood.
controls.r: Assess likelihood and magnitude of impacts, incl. via consultation with affected communities where relevant.

controls.title: Risk treatments, incl. response and recovery, and communication plans for the identified and measured AI risks are documented and monitored regularly.
controls.r: Establish and test incident response/recovery plans for AI-related incidents; maintain communication plans for affected stakeholders and authorities.
controls.e: AI incident response/recovery plan, communication plan, test/exercise records

controls.title: Terms, definitions and overview of AI system impact assessment (AISIA)
controls.r: Adopt the standard's terminology (AI system impact assessment, affected stakeholder, AI actor, etc.) and understand its purpose: assessing how an AI system and its foreseeable applications may affect individuals, groups and society acros...

controls.title: Purpose and scope of the AISIA process
controls.r: Establish why and for which AI systems/use cases the organization will perform impact assessments, and how the process applies across sizes/types of organization.

controls.title: Roles and responsibilities
controls.r: Assign roles for conducting, reviewing and approving impact assessments (e.g. assessors, AI system owner, independent reviewer, affected-party liaison).

controls.title: Triggers and timing across the AI system lifecycle
controls.r: Determine when an AISIA is performed or updated: initial design, before deployment, on significant change, periodically in operation, and at decommissioning.
controls.e: AISIA trigger criteria, lifecycle checkpoint schedule

controls.title: Identifying affected stakeholders
controls.r: Identify individuals, groups, communities and society that could be affected by the AI system, directly or indirectly.

controls.title: Identifying potential impacts
controls.r: Identify potential positive and negative impacts (e.g. on rights, safety, fairness, autonomy, economic, environmental, security-related harms) arising from intended and foreseeable use.

controls.title: Determining and implementing mitigation actions
controls.r: Identify options to prevent, reduce or otherwise address negative impacts, decide and implement appropriate actions, and record residual impact.
controls.e: Mitigation action plan, residual impact sign-off

controls.title: Review, monitoring and reassessment
controls.r: Monitor the AI system and its context for change, and review/update the impact assessment periodically or when triggers in 5.3 occur.

controls.title: Content of the impact assessment record
controls.r: Document scope, context, affected stakeholders, identified impacts, analysis/evaluation, decisions, mitigation actions and residual impacts, and who approved the assessment.

controls.title: Communication of results
controls.r: Determine what impact assessment information is communicated to interested parties (e.g. management, regulators, affected stakeholders) and how.
controls.e: Communication plan/records, published summaries where applicable

controls.title: Guidance for use with ISO/IEC 42001

controls.title: AI system impact assessment template
controls.r: Use or adapt the standard's AISIA template to structure and document individual assessments consistently across the organization.

controls.title: Conduct a privacy/data protection impact assessment for the design
controls.r: Perform a DPIA/PIA (or AI system impact assessment for AI features) as part of the design process for any processing likely to pose meaningful privacy risk, and feed findings back into the design.
controls.e: DPIA/AISIA reports linked to design decisions

controls.title: Assess both positive and negative impacts arising from regular use
controls.r: Examine impacts the AI system has in practice - beneficial and harmful - on the people and groups who interact with it, feeding results back into the AI System Impact Assessment (Tab 6, ISO 42005) and AI RMF Map function (Tab 5).
controls.e: Field-testing impact findings cross-referenced to the ISO 42005 impact assessment

controls.title: Treat ARIA results as research input, not a compliance record

controls.e: Internal note on how ARIA outcomes feed into, but do not replace, existing risk/impact assessments

controls.title: AI system operation and monitoring
controls.r: Define and document elements for ongoing operation: system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.
controls.e: Monitoring dashboards, drift/performance alerts, update procedures

controls.title: AI system recording of event logs
controls.r: Determine at which phases of the life cycle event logs should be enabled, at minimum when the system is in use.

controls.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
controls.r: Determine what needs monitoring/measuring, methods, timing and responsibilities; evaluate AI performance and AIMS effectiveness; retain evidence.

controls.title: Management review inputs
controls.r: Consider status of previous actions, changes in issues, AIMS performance (NCs, monitoring, audits, objectives), interested-party feedback, opportunities for improvement and risks.

controls.title: Record-keeping (logging)
controls.r: Design high-risk AI systems with capability for automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime to ensure traceability appropriate to intended purpose.
controls.e: Logging design spec, log retention records

controls.title: Risk (top-level definition)

controls.title: Loss Event Frequency (LEF)

controls.title: Threat Capability (TCap)

controls.e: Control strength estimate for the controls protecting the asset in scope

controls.title: Vulnerability (Vuln)

controls.r: Combine Threat Event Frequency and Vulnerability to derive the probable frequency of actual loss events for the scenario.

controls.title: Stage 3 / Step 9 - Estimate probable loss magnitude
controls.r: Estimate the probable (most likely range of) loss magnitude for the scenario, considering primary and secondary loss across the six forms of loss (see T.7-T.8).
controls.e: Probable loss magnitude estimate (distribution) per scenario

controls.title: Stage 4 / Step 10 - Derive and articulate risk
controls.r: Combine the Loss Event Frequency and Probable Loss Magnitude distributions (typically via Monte Carlo simulation) to produce a risk result - e.g. a loss exceedance curve or annualized loss expectancy range - and communicate it in busines...
controls.e: Risk model output (loss exceedance curve / ALE range) and executive-level risk articulation

controls.title: Use calibrated estimation techniques
controls.r: Train analysts in calibrated estimation (e.g. the 90% confidence-interval calibration training common in FAIR practice) so subjective range estimates are statistically defensible rather than arbitrary.
controls.e: Calibration training records for risk analysts

controls.title: Maintain a consistent FAIR taxonomy and glossary
controls.r: Ensure all analysts use the same FAIR definitions (per the FAIR taxonomy standard, e.g. Open FAIR O-RT) so risk scenarios are comparable across the organization and over time.

controls.title: Privacy and protection of PII
controls.r: Identify and meet requirements for privacy and PII protection per law and contract.
controls.e: Privacy policy, ROPA, DPIAs, DSAR process

controls.title: Definitions
controls.r: Apply GDPR definitions consistently (personal data, processing, controller, processor, consent, special categories, pseudonymisation, etc.).

controls.title: Lawfulness of processing
controls.r: Identify and document a valid legal basis for each processing activity (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests).

controls.title: Conditions for consent
controls.r: Where relying on consent, ensure it is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable, and as easy to withdraw as to give.

controls.title: Conditions for children's consent
controls.r: Apply age-of-consent rules for information society services offered directly to children, incl. parental consent verification where required.

controls.title: Special categories of personal data
controls.r: Do not process special-category data (health, biometric, genetic, racial/ethnic origin, etc.) unless an Article 9(2) condition applies; apply enhanced safeguards.
controls.e: Special-category processing register and conditions relied on

controls.title: Processing of criminal conviction/offence data
controls.r: Only process such data under official authority or with appropriate safeguards.
controls.e: Legal basis and safeguards for criminal-data processing

controls.title: Data protection by design and by default
controls.r: Implement data protection principles (e.g. pseudonymisation, minimisation) by design at the time of determining processing means, and by default ensure only necessary data is processed.

controls.title: General principle for transfers / adequacy decisions
controls.r: Transfer personal data outside the EEA only where an adequacy decision applies or another Chapter V mechanism is used.

controls.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
controls.r: Absent adequacy, use appropriate safeguards (e.g. Standard Contractual Clauses, Binding Corporate Rules) providing enforceable rights and effective remedies.

controls.title: Derogations for specific situations
controls.r: Rely on derogations (explicit consent, contract necessity, public interest, etc.) only where Article 46 mechanisms are unavailable and conditions are met.

controls.title: PII sharing, transfer and disclosure
controls.r: Identify the basis for transfers between jurisdictions/organizations; document and communicate applicable transfer mechanisms; record and manage disclosures to third parties, incl. legally mandated disclosures.
controls.e: Transfer/disclosure register, cross-border transfer mechanism records (e.g. SCCs)

controls.title: Conditions for collection and processing
controls.r: Process PII only per documented instructions of the controller (incl. for transfers); ensure the contract with the controller addresses PII processing; assist the controller in fulfilling its obligations.

controls.title: PII sharing, transfer and disclosure
controls.r: Notify the controller of legally binding requests for disclosure, of any unauthorized access/breach, and of the use of sub-processors; disclose/transfer PII only per controller instructions and applicable transfer mechanisms.
controls.e: Sub-processor notifications, breach notification to controller, disclosure records

controls.title: Design around the interests of the individual, not just the organization
controls.r: Make user-centric choices the default in the design: strong privacy defaults, clear consent flows, and easy-to-find control over one's own data.
controls.e: User-centric design review, usability testing on privacy controls

controls.title: Give individuals meaningful control over their own data
controls.r: Provide accessible mechanisms within the design for individuals to access, correct, export or delete their data and withdraw consent, without undue friction.
controls.e: Self-service privacy controls (access, correction, deletion, export, consent withdrawal) built into the product

controls.title: AI risk treatment
controls.r: Define AI risk treatment process: select options, determine necessary controls (compare with Annex A), produce Statement of Applicability with justification, formulate treatment plan, obtain approval and residual risk acceptance.
controls.e: AI risk treatment plan, SoA, residual risk sign-off

controls.title: Data for development and enhancement of AI system
controls.r: Define, document and implement data management processes related to AI development.

controls.title: Compliance with the requirements
controls.r: Ensure high-risk AI systems comply with Articles 9-15 throughout their lifecycle, considering intended purpose and generally acknowledged state of the art.

controls.title: Policies, processes, procedures and practices for mapping, measuring and managing AI risk are established, documented and effectively implemented, reflecting organizational risk tolerance.
controls.r: Establish AI risk-management policies/processes covering legal/regulatory requirements, and review/update them regularly.
controls.e: AI risk management policy, process documentation, review log

controls.title: Context is established and understood: intended purpose, business value, risk tolerances, requirements, and impacted stakeholders identified.
controls.r: Document AI system context: purpose, users, requirements (incl. legal/regulatory and security requirements).

controls.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
controls.r: Identify, document and keep current legal/regulatory/contractual requirements and how they are met.

controls.title: Intellectual property rights
controls.r: Implement procedures to protect intellectual property rights.

controls.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
controls.r: Define, enforce and communicate security duties that remain valid after termination/change.

controls.title: Legal and contractual matters
controls.r: The CB is a legal entity and has a legally enforceable certification agreement with each client, defining rights/obligations and responsibility for decisions.

controls.title: Cooperation with the supervisory authority
controls.r: Cooperate with the supervisory authority on request in the performance of its tasks.

controls.title: Prior consultation
controls.r: Consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a DPIA indicates high residual risk that cannot be mitigated.

controls.title: Administrative fines
controls.r: Ensure compliance to avoid fines (tiered, up to the higher of EUR 20m or 4% of global annual turnover for the most serious infringements).

controls.title: Ensure secure retention and disposal
controls.r: Define and enforce retention periods per data category, and ensure secure, verifiable destruction or anonymisation of personal data once no longer needed.

controls.title: Supervisory powers and penalties
controls.r: Be aware competent authorities can order cessation of non-compliant conduct, impose administrative penalties (on the entity and responsible natural persons), and publish penalty/measure information (naming and shaming); some Member State...
controls.e: Legal/compliance risk register reflecting DORA penalty exposure

controls.title: Understand ARIA is not a certification or compliance programme
controls.r: Confirm internally that participation or alignment with ARIA does not constitute certification, regulatory compliance, or an official safety approval - it is a research evaluation environment whose results are published for the AI commun...
controls.e: Internal communication clarifying ARIA is non-certifying

controls.title: Validate the methodology periodically against the Open Group's requirements for risk assessment methodologies
controls.r: Periodically check that the organization's FAIR implementation still satisfies the general quality criteria for a sound risk methodology (clearly defined, internally consistent taxonomy; ability to express variability/uncertainty with ra...
controls.e: Periodic internal review of FAIR implementation against these quality criteria

controls.title: Reconnaissance
controls.r: Adversary gathers information about the target AI/ML system to plan the attack: system capabilities, system prompts, access controls, data sources, competitive/proprietary details.
controls.e: Test for prompt/system-prompt extraction, RBAC enumeration, and disclosure of proprietary or competitive information

controls.title: Resource Development
controls.r: Adversary creates, purchases or compromises resources (malicious prompts, tools, infrastructure) to support the attack - a preparatory stage before the target system is touched.
controls.e: Threat intelligence monitoring for adversary tooling/infrastructure relevant to the organization's AI systems

controls.title: Initial Access
controls.r: Adversary gains an initial foothold in the AI/ML system via entry vectors such as input validation weaknesses, prompt injection, SQL/shell injection, SSRF, or exposed debug endpoints.
controls.e: Input validation testing, prompt-injection testing, debug-endpoint exposure checks (cross-ref OWASP LLM01, Tab 10)

controls.title: AI Model Access
controls.r: Adversary obtains some level of access to the AI model itself - ranging from full internal knowledge (white-box) to only inference-API access (black-box) - which shapes what further attacks are feasible.
controls.e: Model access-boundary review: confirm what level of model access is exposed to which parties

controls.title: Privilege Escalation
controls.r: Adversary gains higher-level permissions than originally obtained, e.g. escalating from inference-API access to pipeline or infrastructure control.
controls.e: Least-privilege review of AI pipeline/service accounts and escalation-path testing

controls.title: Defense Evasion
controls.r: Adversary avoids detection or conceals malicious actions within the AI system, making them appear as normal behaviour (e.g. subtle poisoning below detection thresholds).
controls.e: Detection-threshold review and anomaly-detection tuning for subtle/low-and-slow AI-specific manipulation

controls.title: Credential Access
controls.r: Adversary steals account names, passwords, API keys or tokens used to access AI systems/services.
controls.e: Credential/secret-management review for AI pipeline and inference-API access (cross-ref ISO 27001 8.2/8.5, Tab 7)

controls.title: Discovery
controls.r: Adversary maps the AI environment - available models, datasets, tools, APIs and their configuration - to plan further action.
controls.e: Environment/asset exposure review for AI-related infrastructure discoverable by an attacker

controls.title: Lateral Movement
controls.r: Adversary moves from the initially compromised component to other parts of the AI system or connected environment (e.g. from an agent's tool access into a connected backend system).
controls.e: Network/service segmentation testing between AI components and the broader environment (cross-ref ISO 27001 8.22, Tab 7)

controls.title: Collection
controls.r: Adversary gathers data of interest from the AI system - training data, user inputs, outputs, or embeddings - in preparation for exfiltration or further use.
controls.e: Data access logging and anomalous-collection-pattern monitoring around AI data stores

controls.title: AI Attack Staging
controls.r: Adversary prepares and positions an AI-specific attack: poisoning inputs/training data, crafting adversarial examples, embedding backdoors, or inducing hallucinations for exploitation - the tactic with the most AI-native techniques and n...
controls.e: Adversarial-input and data-poisoning testing (cross-ref OWASP LLM01/LLM04/LLM06, Tab 10, and ISO 27090 Clause 6, Tab 21)

controls.title: Command and Control
controls.r: Adversary establishes a channel to communicate with and control a compromised AI component remotely.
controls.e: Egress monitoring and anomalous outbound-connection detection from AI infrastructure

controls.title: Exfiltration
controls.r: Adversary steals data out of the AI system - PII, training data, proprietary prompts, or other sensitive information - including via encoded/obfuscated channels to evade data-loss prevention.
controls.e: DLP tuned for AI-specific exfiltration channels (inference responses, encoded outputs) (cross-ref ISO 27001 8.12, Tab 7)

controls.title: Impact
controls.r: Adversary disrupts, degrades, destroys the AI system or manipulates its outputs - hijacking its purpose, generating harmful content, causing unauthorized actions, or taking excessive agency.
controls.e: Impact-scenario red-teaming: hijacking, excessive-agency and output-manipulation testing (cross-ref OWASP LLM06, Tab 10)

controls.title: Processes for responsible AI system design and development
controls.r: Define and document specific processes for responsible design and development of AI systems.

controls.title: AI roles and responsibilities
controls.r: Define and allocate AI roles and responsibilities per organizational needs.
controls.e: AI governance roles, RACI, committee charter

controls.title: Reporting of concerns
controls.r: Define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

controls.title: Customers
controls.r: Ensure the organization's responsible AI approach considers customer expectations and needs.

controls.title: General documentation requirements
controls.r: Determine what information must be documented for each AISIA to support transparency, accountability and traceability of the process and its outcomes.

controls.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
controls.r: Define and allocate security roles per organizational needs.

controls.title: Accountability
controls.r: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the principles.
controls.e: Records of processing, policies, evidence of compliance mechanisms

controls.title: Responsibility of the controller
controls.r: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate processing complies with the Regulation, proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Joint controllers
controls.r: Determine and transparently document respective responsibilities of joint controllers via an arrangement.

controls.title: Representatives of controllers/processors not established in the Union
controls.r: Designate an EU representative where required by territorial scope.

controls.title: Tasks of the DPO
controls.r: DPO informs/advises on obligations, monitors compliance, advises on DPIAs, cooperates with and acts as contact point for the supervisory authority.

controls.title: Assigning relevant roles and authorities
controls.r: Assign clear roles and decision-making authority for privacy-by-design activities across the organization (e.g. product, engineering, legal, security).

controls.title: Accountability for providing privacy information
controls.r: Assign clear accountability within the organization for ensuring privacy information given to consumers is accurate, current and properly delivered.
controls.e: Accountable owner for consumer privacy communications

controls.title: Quality of data for AI systems
controls.r: Define and document data quality requirements and ensure data used meets them.
controls.e: Data quality criteria and check results

controls.title: Data resources
controls.r: Document information about data resources used for the AI system.

controls.title: Acquisition of data
controls.r: Determine and document details about acquisition and selection of data used in AI systems.
controls.e: Data acquisition records, licences, consent basis

controls.title: Data preparation
controls.r: Define and document criteria for selecting data preparation methods and how they are used.

controls.title: Data and data governance
controls.r: Apply data governance practices to training/validation/testing data: relevant design choices, provenance, collection, bias examination, gaps identification, and appropriate quality/representativeness; protect data appropriately.

controls.title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models
controls.r: Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, provide information/documentation to downstream providers, establish a copyright policy, publish a sufficiently detailed training-content summary.
controls.e: GPAI technical documentation, training data summary

controls.title: Robustness, security and safety
controls.r: AI systems should function appropriately and not pose unreasonable safety/security risks throughout their lifecycle; traceability of datasets, processes and decisions; risk-based approach with continuous risk management (security, safety...
controls.e: Robustness/security testing, risk management process, traceability records, deactivation/kill-switch controls

controls.title: Intellectual property rights
controls.r: Respect intellectual property rights, incl. in relation to training data and generated content.

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.r: The model inadvertently exposes PII, credentials, proprietary data or confidential business information present in training data, context or connected systems.
controls.e: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

controls.title: Supply Chain
controls.r: Compromised or vulnerable components in the LLM supply chain - pre-trained models, fine-tuning adapters (e.g. LoRA), datasets, plugins and deployment platforms - introduce vulnerabilities, backdoors or bias.
controls.e: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

controls.title: Training and operational dataset provenance
controls.r: Apply ISO/IEC 5181's provenance techniques to datasets used for AI training, fine-tuning, RAG/retrieval and evaluation, recording source, collection method, licensing and every transformation the dataset underwent before use.
controls.e: Dataset provenance records cross-referenced to the Data Governance Register (Tab 19) and ISO 42001 A.7.5 (Tabs 1-2)

controls.title: Model lineage and versioning provenance
controls.r: Record the provenance of the AI model itself: base model(s) used, fine-tuning datasets and steps applied, version history, and who/what performed each step - distinct from but complementary to the data-level provenance in AI.1.
controls.e: Model card / model lineage register with provenance metadata per version

controls.title: Provenance for third-party and supply-chain AI components
controls.r: Extend provenance capture to third-party models, datasets, libraries and APIs incorporated into an AI system, consistent with the AI supply-chain controls already tracked elsewhere in this workbook (ISO 42001 A.10, Tab 1-2; EU AI Act val...

controls.title: Physical security perimeters
controls.r: Define and use security perimeters to protect areas with information and assets.

controls.title: Physical entry
controls.r: Protect secure areas with entry controls and access points.

controls.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
controls.r: Design and implement physical security for offices, rooms and facilities.

controls.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
controls.r: Design and implement protection against fire, flood, and other natural or man-made threats.

controls.title: Working in secure areas
controls.r: Design and implement security measures for working in secure areas.

controls.title: Clear desk and clear screen
controls.r: Define and enforce clear desk (papers/media) and clear screen rules.

controls.title: Equipment siting and protection
controls.r: Site and protect equipment to reduce environmental risks and unauthorized access.

controls.title: Security of assets off-premises
controls.r: Protect off-site assets.

controls.title: Storage media
controls.r: Manage storage media through acquisition, use, transport and disposal per classification.

controls.title: Cabling security
controls.r: Protect power/data/service cabling from interception, interference or damage.

controls.title: Equipment maintenance
controls.r: Maintain equipment correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality.

controls.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
controls.r: Verify data and licensed software are removed/overwritten before disposal or re-use.

controls.title: Physical controls - privacy guidance
controls.r: Apply privacy-specific guidance to physical controls (e.g. secure areas/media handling where PII is stored or processed physically).
controls.e: Physical control review for locations holding PII

controls.title: Confidentiality and access control of assessment records
controls.r: Control access to AISIA documentation appropriately, since records may contain sensitive information about individuals, vulnerabilities or system design.

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.r: Segregate conflicting duties and areas of responsibility.

controls.title: Access control
controls.r: Establish and implement rules to control physical and logical access based on business and security requirements.

controls.title: Identity management
controls.r: Manage the full life cycle of identities.

controls.title: Authentication information
controls.r: Control allocation and management of authentication information incl. user guidance.

controls.title: Access rights
controls.r: Provision, review, modify and remove access rights per policy.

controls.title: Privileged access rights
controls.r: Restrict and manage allocation and use of privileged access rights.
controls.e: PAM (e.g. CyberArk) records, privileged access reviews

controls.title: Information access restriction
controls.r: Restrict access to information and assets per access control policy.

controls.title: Secure authentication
controls.r: Implement secure authentication technologies and procedures based on access restrictions.

controls.title: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor
controls.r: Ensure persons processing data under the controller's/processor's authority do so only on instructions, unless required by law.

controls.title: Demonstrate that privacy and security reinforce each other
controls.r: Show, for security-relevant features, how the chosen design serves both security and privacy objectives together (e.g. access control that both secures data and limits who can see personal data).
controls.e: Combined privacy/security design rationale for key features

controls.title: Key contractual provisions
controls.r: Ensure contracts for critical/important functions include mandatory provisions: service description, data locations, data protection, availability/security, audit and access rights, termination rights, reporting, data portability, and su...
controls.e: Contract clause checklist against Art.30(2) mandatory provisions

controls.title: AI policy
controls.r: Establish, document, communicate and make available an AI policy appropriate to the organization's purpose, providing a framework for AI objectives, committing to applicable requirements and continual improvement; consistent with other p...

controls.title: Continual improvement
controls.r: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AIMS.

controls.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
controls.r: React to NCs, evaluate need to eliminate causes, implement and review corrective action effectiveness, update AIMS; retain evidence.

controls.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
controls.r: Take corrective actions or withdraw/recall a non-conforming system; inform distributors, deployers, authorised representative and, where relevant, authorities of the non-conformity and actions taken.

controls.title: Obligations of distributors
controls.r: Verify CE marking, documentation and conformity before making a system available; not make available if non-conforming; take corrective action if aware of non-conformity.

controls.title: Policy
controls.r: Establish an information security policy suited to the purpose, providing objectives/framework, commitment to requirements and continual improvement; documented, communicated, available to interested parties.

controls.title: Continual improvement
controls.r: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS.

controls.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
controls.r: React to NCs, evaluate need to eliminate causes, implement and review corrective action for effectiveness, update ISMS; retain evidence.

controls.title: Conducting audits
controls.r: Opening/closing meetings, evidence gathering and verification, recording findings (nonconformities and opportunities for improvement), audit report, cause analysis of nonconformities and verification of corrections/corrective actions.
controls.e: Audit evidence, corrective action plans, root-cause analyses

controls.title: Option A - Corrective actions
controls.r: The CB identifies and manages nonconformities and takes corrective action.

controls.title: Option A - Preventive actions
controls.r: The CB takes actions to eliminate causes of potential nonconformities (risk-based).

controls.title: Improvement (privacy extension)
controls.r: Extend ISO 27001 10.1-10.2 continual improvement and corrective action to nonconformities affecting the PIMS.

controls.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Design and develop high-risk AI systems to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, perform consistently, and be resilient to errors, faults, inconsistencies, and attempts by unauthorised third parties to exp...
controls.e: Robustness/security test reports, resilience measures, cybersecurity controls

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Manipulation of training, fine-tuning or embedding data introduces vulnerabilities, backdoors or biases that compromise the model's security, effectiveness or ethical behaviour.
controls.e: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Weaknesses in how vectors/embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved (e.g. in RAG pipelines) allow injection of malicious content, data poisoning of the knowledge base, or unauthorized retrieval of restricted data.
controls.e: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

controls.title: Data poisoning
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Deliberate injection of false, mislabelled or manipulated data into training/fine-tuning data to corrupt the resulting model's behaviour.
controls.e: Data provenance/integrity controls on training data (cross-ref Tab 19 Data Governance Register, Tab 20 ISO 5181)

controls.title: Model poisoning
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Deliberate manipulation of the model itself (e.g. during training, fine-tuning, or via a compromised supply-chain component) to embed a backdoor or degrade behaviour.
controls.e: Model training pipeline integrity controls, signed/verified model artifacts

controls.title: Evasion
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Deliberately crafted training or prompt inputs designed to mislead the AI algorithm at inference time (adversarial examples, adversarial prompts).
controls.e: Adversarial robustness testing (cross-ref OWASP LLM01 Prompt Injection, Tab 10)

controls.title: Membership inference
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Techniques to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training data, potentially revealing sensitive information about individuals in the training set.
controls.e: Membership-inference testing as part of model privacy/security evaluation

controls.title: Model inversion
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Techniques to reconstruct or infer characteristics of training data points from a model's outputs or parameters, potentially recovering sensitive underlying data.
controls.e: Model inversion resistance testing (e.g. output perturbation, differential privacy)

controls.title: Model stealing (extraction)
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Theft of the valuable intellectual property embodied in a trained model - the model itself, its training data, and its inputs/prompts - typically via systematic querying.
controls.e: Rate limiting, query monitoring and IP-protection controls (cross-ref OWASP LLM10 Unbounded Consumption, Tab 10)

controls.title: Prompt injection and output injection
controls.d: ISO 27090 / OWASP AI Threat Catalogue (Poisoning, Evasion, Extraction, Injection)
controls.r: Downstream attacks exploiting vulnerabilities in operational AI systems: injecting malicious instructions via prompts, or injecting malicious content via the model's output into systems that consume it.
controls.e: Input/output validation and sanitization controls (cross-ref OWASP LLM01/LLM05, Tab 10)

controls.title: Governance and organisation
controls.r: The management body bears ultimate responsibility for ICT risk: defines risk appetite, approves ICT security policies and the ICT risk management framework, approves ICT budget/staffing/training, approves major ICT projects, ensures a cr...
controls.e: Board-approved ICT risk appetite, policies, budget and project approvals; board reporting line on ICT risk

controls.title: ICT risk management framework
controls.r: Maintain a robust, well-documented ICT risk management framework (strategies, policies, procedures, protocols, tools) that minimises the impact of ICT risk; document and review the function periodically, after major incidents, and at lea...
controls.e: ICT RMF documentation, annual/post-incident review records

controls.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
controls.r: Use ICT systems/protocols/tools that are appropriate to operations, reliable under stress/peak load, technologically resilient, and kept up to date with security standards (patched/maintained).
controls.e: Technology standards, patch/maintenance records, capacity/stress-test evidence

controls.title: Backup policies and procedures
controls.r: Maintain backup policies specifying frequency, type and location/scope of backups; keep restoration systems separate from the primary system and activatable without undue delay; test restorability so restore times align with RTOs; cloud-...
controls.e: Backup policy, restoration testing records aligned to RTO

controls.title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
controls.r: Small and less complex entities may apply a simplified ICT RMF covering key risk-management elements, simplified testing and simplified reporting, per the applicable regulatory technical standards.

controls.title: Advanced testing based on threat-led penetration testing (TLPT)
controls.r: Entities meeting applicability criteria perform TLPT at least every three years, on live production systems, covering critical/important functions, using cyber threat intelligence to develop realistic attack scenarios; results are mutual...
controls.e: TLPT scope, scenario design based on threat intelligence, TLPT report

controls.title: Requirements for TLPT testers
controls.r: Testers must demonstrate methodology capability and technical expertise, hold relevant professional certifications, and have no conflict of interest with the tested entity.

controls.title: General principles for managing ICT third-party risk
controls.r: Adopt, review and update an ICT third-party risk policy; record all ICT service arrangements in a Register of Information (submitted at least annually to the competent authority); perform pre-contractual due diligence for critical/import...
controls.e: ICT third-party risk policy, Register of Information, due-diligence and monitoring records, exit strategies

controls.title: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level
controls.r: Assess, before entering a new ICT service arrangement, the entity-level concentration risk, including the risk that entire ICT services could become unavailable due to reliance on a single provider.
controls.e: Concentration-risk assessment per new/renewed ICT arrangement

controls.title: Designation of critical ICT third-party service providers (CTPPs)
controls.r: Be aware that the European Supervisory Authorities designate certain ICT third-party providers as 'critical' based on defined criteria; non-EU critical providers must designate an EU legal representative.
controls.e: Awareness of CTPP status of key providers used

controls.title: Understanding the organization and its context
controls.r: Determine external/internal issues relevant to the AIMS purpose and to achieving its intended results, incl. the organization's role(s) (provider, producer, user, etc.) and applicable AI-related climate/regulatory factors.
controls.e: Context analysis, AI role determination, issue register

controls.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
controls.r: Determine whether an AI system is high-risk: safety component of a regulated product (Annex I) or use case listed in Annex III, with a narrow self-assessment exemption where risk is not significant.

controls.title: Amendments to Annex III
controls.r: Monitor Commission updates to the high-risk use-case list (Annex III) and re-assess systems accordingly.

controls.title: High-risk AI system use cases
controls.r: Check whether the AI system falls under a listed high-risk use case (biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services incl. access to insurance/credit, law enforcement, migration/asylum/border, justice/democ...

controls.title: Categorization of the AI system is performed, incl. specific tasks and methods used to implement them.
controls.r: Categorize the AI system by task, method (e.g. classification, generative), and risk level.

controls.title: AI capabilities, targeted usage, goals and expected benefits/costs are understood compared with appropriate benchmarks.
controls.r: Document expected AI system performance and benchmarks; consider failure/edge cases.

controls.title: Understanding the organization and its context
controls.r: Determine external/internal issues relevant to ISMS purpose and intended outcomes.

controls.title: Determining the scope of the ISMS

controls.r: The CB must be impartial and be seen to be; decisions are based on objective evidence, free from conflicts of interest.
